analysis.title: GS Materials - Nov 18...Copper WEBCAST 9am (replay available), ...
key_insights: Copper traded poorly on 18 Nov with the dollar higher (DXY 103.76) and the US 10-year at 5.09%. The desk heard margin calls in base and precious metals and could not point to a single catalyst.

China copper open interest rose 5% (30k lots) on very light volumes, which the desk compares to mid-2025 levels. China physical premiums keep rising to record highs. SHFE is short, meaning open interest exceeds the metal available for delivery.
Warrant stocks are picking up from a very low base. The desk says the arbitrage points to metal moving from COMEX into Shanghai, and it is watching New Orleans (NOLA).
China and CTAs are positioned short copper, and Druckenmiller said he is short. The desk notes he did not say he sold yesterday and suspects a trader may be starting to cover at these levels.

Copper smelter benchmark: the desk has heard a negative benchmark of -$50 to -$100 (CRU) and also -$50 to -$150, with sources on the ground saying either side of -$100 is achievable. Top smelters are still profitable at -$118. A deeper negative benchmark squeezes marginal smelters and would reduce cathode production. Who sets the benchmark is unclear, and some suggest FCX may lead.
The desk points to the power grid as the place to watch for real copper demand. China has the generation capacity but needs connection and distribution. It names 600406.CH as a stock to watch.
China trade data: copper output +1.8% y/y at 1.22mt, zinc output -9.7% y/y at 604kt, rare earth exports +5.5% y/y at 11kt, alumina exports +39.9% y/y at 250kt.

A China materials monitor says metal price volatility and the copper physical premium caused the first order-book pushback from end users in months. Domestic copper scrap disruption is deep and unchanged, and further smelter output cuts remain a risk. Chinese demand in the first half of November was 2-10% lower y/y for cement, flat and construction steel, and 2% higher for copper and aluminium.

Anglo American: Brazil told the European Commission that its review of the sale of the Brazilian nickel mine to MMG is unwelcome interference. The Anglo CEO said that if the deal is prohibited, ferronickel volumes from Barro Alto and Codemin would be withdrawn permanently, and that the status quo is not the alternative. The desk flags 21 Dec as the date to watch.
BHP is selling West Musgrave (nickel, copper). The desk says the more interesting question is whether East Coast coal assets are for sale, which matters for both BHP and Glencore.

Glencore: ERG will split into two businesses, one focused on global critical minerals. Mutalip is the buyer of Kazzinc, a 70% stake that consensus values at $4.0-4.5bn (FT said up to $5bn). The Glencore CEO said in October that completion would take 30-60 days, and the desk's source called that realistic. Zinc has been the best base metal year to date.

First Quantum: the company announced formal talks on a new contract will commence after the President agreed with his ministers' recommendation. The desk says the stock is moving closer to a reopening and the focus is now the economics of the new contract. Ministers are reported to target year end. At C$30 with Cobre fully ramped it trades on 3.5x/2.5x EV/EBITDA and an 11%/21% FCF yield in 2028/29.

Utilities: SSE reported H1 adjusted EPS of 65.5p, in line with its 64-68p trading statement, and reiterated full-year guidance of 168-193p against Bloomberg consensus of 185.6p. Severn Trent beat the desk's PBIT expectation by 2%, helped by a £14m property sale and interest cost timing, and the desk stays Sell.

China A-shares ended slightly higher on turnover below 1.4 Tn RMB, the lowest since July 2025. Chip-control headlines drove sectors. Nvidia is no longer shipping Hopper data center chips to China, and a reported US ban on Chinese optical transceivers had less impact on China optics names than expected.
GS 2027 outlook links include a cut to its 2027 iron ore forecast to about US$90/t.

market_movers.rationale: Severn Trent H1 beat the desk's PBIT expectation by 2%, helped by a £14m property sale and interest cost timing. Sell rating and 12-month target unchanged.

First Quantum announced formal talks to reopen Cobre. The desk sees it moving closer to reopening, with the new contract economics and a possible year-end target the open items. It remains a top ask in copper.
Anglo American says Brazilian ferronickel volumes would be withdrawn permanently if the MMG sale is prohibited by the EU review. The desk flags 21 Dec as the date to watch.

earnings_insights: SSE: H1 2027 adjusted EPS reported at 65.5p, in line with the company's own trading statement range of 64-68p. Full-year 2026/27 adjusted EPS guidance reiterated at 168-193p, against Bloomberg consensus of 185.6p. Full-year capex is expected above £5bn.
Severn Trent: H1 2027 PBIT was about 2% above GS expectations, helped by a £14m property sale. EPS strength versus GS expectations is mainly from timing of interest costs between H2 and H1.

First Quantum: GS valuation at C$30 and spot copper of $13,200 is 3.5x/2.5x EV/EBITDA and 11%/21% FCF yield for 2028/29 with Cobre fully ramped, and 6.3x/5.7x EV/EBITDA and 7.5%/10.5% FCF yield without Cobre. These are GS estimates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Output is still growing modestly despite smelter margin pressure from a deeply negative benchmark.
A sharp annual decline in zinc output.
Exports are up modestly from a year ago.
Alumina exports are sharply higher from a year ago.
GS cut its 2027 iron ore price forecast.

vol_and_positioning: China and CTAs are getting short copper, and Druckenmiller said he is short. The desk suspects some may start covering at current levels.
SHFE copper is short of deliverable metal because open interest exceeds metal available against it.
China copper open interest rose 5% (30k lots) on light volumes comparable to mid-2025.
Margin calls were heard in base and precious metals overnight with no obvious trigger.
geopolitical: US reportedly moving ahead with a ban on Chinese optical transceivers despite pushback from US hyperscalers

tension_points.bull_case: China physical premiums are at record highs, SHFE open interest exceeds deliverable metal, and warrant stocks are low. China and CTAs are short, and the desk suspects Druckenmiller may be starting to cover at current levels.
tension_points.bear_case: The dollar and US rates are rising, margin calls are hitting base and precious metals, China volumes are very light, and Druckenmiller says he is short. Chinese end users have pushed back on orders because of price volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Warrant stocks rising and metal flowing from COMEX into Shanghai, which the desk says the arbitrage points to, would ease the SHFE delivery squeeze.
